category: probability and stochastic processes / stochastic processes
canonical_claim: Let the interarrival law F be a probability distribution on the nonnegative reals with finite positive mean mu, and let U be its renewal measure. In the nonarithmetic case, for every fixed h > 0, U((x, x+h]) tends to h/mu as x tends to infinity. In the arithmetic case of maximal span d > 0, the corresponding span-d renewal masses tend to d/mu along the lattice.
domain_and_universes: A Borel probability law on Real supported on [0, infinity), its convolution renewal measure U = sum over n >= 0 of F convolution powers, real parameters mu, h, x, and a separate arithmetic span d; exact Lean types and universes remain open.
quantifiers: mu = integral t with respect to F, with 0 < mu < infinity
arithmetic branch: maximal span d > 0 and lattice index tending to infinity
hypotheses: interarrivals are represented by convolution powers of one probability law
F is supported on the nonnegative reals
the mean mu is finite and strictly positive
the branch-specific nonarithmetic or maximal-span arithmetic condition
conclusion: Local increments of the renewal measure converge to interval length divided by the mean, with the lattice analogue using the maximal span.

alternate_encodings.target: U(x+h) - U(x) tends to h / mu
alternate_encodings.relationship: expected equal after fixing the cumulative renewal-function endpoint convention

alternate_encodings.target: sum over n >= 0 of probability(S_n in (x, x+h]) tends to h / mu
alternate_encodings.relationship: expected equal by the definition of the renewal measure and justified interchange

excluded_degenerate_cases: mu = 0, infinite mean, signed interarrivals, defective laws, h <= 0, and a nonmaximal lattice span are excluded from the frozen classical claim. Endpoint and atom-at-zero conditions require explicit resolution in the statement phase.
